headline_marked: PM asks [[State Minister Ishraque Hossain to resign]] after firearm display
headline: PM asks State Minister Ishraque Hossain to resign after firearm display
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman reportedly ordered the resignation of the State Minister for Liberation War Affairs following a controversial anti-drug drive in Gendaria.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has reportedly ordered State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain to resign from the cabinet. The directive was given during a meeting at the Secretariat on Sunday afternoon.

The move follows a controversial anti-drug drive in Gendaria on Saturday, where Ishraque Hossain was seen brandishing a firearm. Videos of the incident, which showed the minister and his associates carrying weapons, sparked widespread criticism.

Critics, including members of the BNP and Jamaat-e-Islami, described the display of arms as an 'alarming misuse of authority' and a 'reign of terror.' They argued that a minister should not lead raids personally with weapons.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has launched an investigation into the incident. The DMP's Detective Branch is examining whether the minister's actions violated the 2025 Firearms License Policy, which prohibits using weapons to create fear or annoyance.

In his defense, Ishraque Hossain stated on Facebook that he was participating in a joint social resistance program against drugs. He claimed he brandished the weapon due to potential attacks from drug dealers during the raid.

The incident occurred on the day the Prime Minister himself was conducting surprise inspections of hospitals and educational institutions, leading some to believe the minister's actions overshadowed the PM's positive initiatives.

headline_marked: Former minister Anisul Huq, three others [[taken for health checks]] ahead of remand
headline: Former minister Anisul Huq, three others taken for health checks ahead of remand
summary: Anisul Huq, former law minister, along with Hasanul Haq Inu and two others, were taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for mandatory health examinations before their remand proceedings.
details: Former law minister Anisul Huq, former Dhaka North City Corporation mayor Atiqul Islam, JSD president and former information minister Hasanul Haq Inu, and former Justice A H M Shamsuddin Chowdhury Manik were taken to Dhaka Medical College (DMC) Hospital for health checks.

The individuals were transported to the hospital under the supervision of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and with the cooperation of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) on Sunday afternoon. They underwent preliminary health examinations before being taken back from the hospital.

According to CID sources, the court approved their remand for questioning in two murder cases filed during the July student protests in the capital's Badda and Mirpur police stations. The health checks are a mandatory procedure before a remand can be executed.
A CID inspector stated that health examinations are conducted on all accused individuals before they are taken into remand and again before they are presented in court after interrogation.
